quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
rationale: Section 7 reverses our required ownership direction. Type II Materials expressly include works "created during the Service performance period," IBM owns them, and Type II is the default where nothing is specified — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership with only an irrevocable licence limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" (no modification or sublicensing rights). Conversely, where we do own Type I Materials, we must grant IBM an irrevocable worldwide licence to distribute them externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit our work product beyond performing the Services. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our Content, Customer Components and data (11.6 only allocates responsibility; 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). The redline makes Type I the default, confines IBM ownership to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables, narrows IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services, and adds a Customer Data/no-joint-ownership provision.
